Thane.soil: Laterite and coastal alluvial soils; medium black in some pockets
Thane.irrigation: Ulhas, Vaitarna and Bhatsa rivers; mostly rain-fed paddy
Thane.special: Heavily urbanised; farming survives mainly in the interior and tribal belts
Thane.challenges: Land loss to urbanisation, flooding in the monsoon
Thane.notes: Paddy is grown in the monsoon on small holdings, with vegetables supplying the Mumbai market.

Palghar.soil: Coastal alluvial and laterite; medium black in parts
Palghar.irrigation: Vaitarna and Surya rivers; rain-fed paddy with some well irrigation
Palghar.special: Dahanu-Gholvad chikoo has a GI tag
Palghar.challenges: Cyclone and coastal erosion risk; tribal-area food security
Palghar.notes: Newer district carved out of Thane in 2014. Dahanu is known for chikoo orchards and flower farming.

Raigad.soil: Laterite and coastal soils; red lateritic on hill slopes
Raigad.irrigation: Kundalika, Savitri and Patalganga rivers; rain-fed paddy
Raigad.special: Alibag white onion has a GI tag
Raigad.challenges: Soil erosion on slopes, salinity near the creeks
Raigad.notes: Coastal agriculture of paddy and orchards, with white onion grown around Alibag.

Ratnagiri.soil: Laterite soils, shallow and acidic, poor in organic matter
Ratnagiri.irrigation: Shastri, Vashishti and Kajvi rivers; mostly rain-fed
Ratnagiri.special: Ratnagiri Hapus (Alphonso) mango has a GI tag
Ratnagiri.challenges: Mango flowering is hit by unseasonal rain, steep terrain limits irrigation
Ratnagiri.notes: The heart of Alphonso mango production, with orchards on terraced laterite slopes.

Sindhudurg.rainfall: Very high, roughly 3,000-3,500 mm or more
Sindhudurg.irrigation: Karli, Gad and Terekhol rivers; rain-fed with small check dams
Sindhudurg.special: Devgad mango and Vengurla cashew are well known
Sindhudurg.notes: Maharashtra's southern Konkan district, known for horticulture and cashew processing.

Mumbai City.soil: Reclaimed coastal land; saline and built-up
Mumbai City.special: Fully urban, with no meaningful farmland
Mumbai City.notes: Included so the map is complete; it has negligible agriculture.

Mumbai Suburban.soil: Coastal and built-up; some marshy land
Mumbai Suburban.notes: Almost no agriculture beyond small urban or community gardens.

Nashik.soil: Medium to deep black (basalt) in the east; shallow and red-brown in the western hills
Nashik.rainfall: Varies widely: about 500 mm in the east to over 2,500 mm in Igatpuri-Peth-Surgana
Nashik.irrigation: Godavari, Girna and Darna rivers; Gangapur and Darna dams; extensive drip irrigation
Nashik.special: Nashik grapes have a GI tag, and Lasalgaon is a major onion market
Nashik.challenges: Hailstorms and unseasonal rain damage grapes, and onion prices swing
Nashik.notes: India's wine-grape capital, with a mix of horticulture and cash crops.

Dhule.irrigation: Tapi, Panzara and Burai rivers; many small irrigation projects
Dhule.special: Dry cotton and millet belt in north-west Maharashtra
Dhule.challenges: Low and erratic rainfall, groundwater depletion
Dhule.notes: A dry-farming district where cotton and millets dominate, with onions on irrigated land.

Nandurbar.soil: Medium black and shallow soils at the foot of the Satpura hills
Nandurbar.irrigation: Tapi and Narmada rivers; Shivan and other small projects
Nandurbar.special: Nandurbar is a major chilli trading centre
Nandurbar.notes: A tribal district in the north-west where cotton and chilli are the main cash crops.

Jalgaon.soil: Deep black soils of the Tapi valley (alluvial and black)
Jalgaon.irrigation: Tapi, Girna and Purna rivers; Hatnur dam; widespread drip irrigation
Jalgaon.special: Banana belt of India; Jalgaon Bharit brinjal has a GI tag
Jalgaon.challenges: Summer heat waves and cold-wave damage to banana, water stress
Jalgaon.notes: Famous for tissue-culture banana, which is exported from here.

Ahilyanagar.soil: Medium to deep black soils; shallow in the drier east
Ahilyanagar.rainfall: Mixed, roughly 400-600 mm in the east to about 1,000 mm in Akole
Ahilyanagar.irrigation: Godavari, Pravara and Mula rivers; Bhandardara and Mula dams
Ahilyanagar.special: Cooperative sugar factories and the agricultural university at Rahuri
Ahilyanagar.challenges: Drought in the east, unequal water sharing
Ahilyanagar.notes: Formerly Ahmednagar. It is Maharashtra's largest district by area, with a sugar-cooperative belt.

Pune.soil: Medium to deep black in valleys; shallow and red in the hills and ghat areas
Pune.rainfall: Wide range: about 400-500 mm in the east to over 2,000 mm in the western ghats
Pune.irrigation: Bhima, Mula-Mutha, Indrayani and Nira rivers; Khadakwasla and Pawna dams
Pune.special: Known for Ambemohar and Indrayani rice (Maval-Mulshi) and Purandar figs
Pune.notes: Mixed farming: sugarcane in the Nira-Bhima belt, rice in the west, and flowers and vegetables near the city.

Satara.soil: Deep black along the Krishna; red and laterite on the western ghats
Satara.rainfall: Extreme range: about 400-500 mm in the east to several thousand mm at Mahabaleshwar
Satara.irrigation: Krishna, Koyna, Venna and Yerala rivers; Koyna dam
Satara.special: Mahabaleshwar strawberry has a GI tag
Satara.challenges: Drought in the eastern talukas (Man, Khatav), landslides in the west
Satara.notes: Strawberries in the hills and sugarcane and groundnut in the plains.

Sangli.soil: Medium to deep black (Krishna and Warna); light, shallow soil in drought-prone Jat
Sangli.rainfall: Roughly 400-500 mm in the east to over 1,000 mm in Shirala
Sangli.irrigation: Krishna, Warna and Yerala rivers; Tembhu and Mhaisal lift schemes
Sangli.special: A major turmeric market, and Tasgaon is known for grapes and raisins (bedana)
Sangli.challenges: Floods along the Krishna, drought in Jat and Atpadi
Sangli.notes: Sugarcane in the river valley, and grapes and turmeric as high-value crops.

Solapur.soil: Deep black (Bhima and Sina valleys); shallow light soils in the west
Solapur.irrigation: Bhima and Sina rivers; Ujani dam is the lifeline
Solapur.special: Solapur pomegranate has a GI tag, and the district is one of the top pomegranate exporters
Solapur.challenges: Chronic water scarcity, rain-fed rabi sowing depends on soil moisture
Solapur.notes: A dry district where rabi jowar and drip-irrigated pomegranate are the signature crops.

Kolhapur.soil: Deep black along the rivers; laterite and red soils in the west
Kolhapur.rainfall: Roughly 600 mm in the east to 2,500 mm or more in the west (Gaganbawda higher)
Kolhapur.irrigation: Krishna, Panchganga, Warna and Dudhganga rivers; Radhanagari dam
Kolhapur.special: Kolhapuri jaggery (gul) and cooperative sugar factories
Kolhapur.challenges: Floods (2019 and 2021), pest pressure on sugarcane
Kolhapur.notes: Among the highest-yielding sugarcane districts, with a fertile Krishna-Panchganga basin.

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.soil: Medium black; shallow in the hilly areas
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.irrigation: Godavari river; Jayakwadi dam (Paithan) and canals
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.special: Marathwada Kesar mango has a GI tag
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.notes: Formerly Aurangabad. Jayakwadi water has made horticulture viable here.

Jalna.irrigation: Godavari, Dudhna and Kundalika; Jayakwadi canal is a partial source
Jalna.special: A leading mosambi district and known as a seed-industry hub
Jalna.notes: Cotton and soybean on rain-fed land, with mosambi orchards where irrigation is available.

Beed.soil: Medium black; shallow in the Balaghat hills
Beed.irrigation: Godavari, Sindphana and Manjara rivers; Majalgaon and Manjara dams
Beed.special: Beed is known for custard apple
Beed.challenges: Drought and farmer distress, seasonal migration of cane cutters
Beed.notes: A drought-prone district with strong dependence on monsoon rainfall.

Latur.irrigation: Manjara, Terna and Tawarja rivers; small dams
Latur.special: A leading soybean and pulses trading and milling hub
Latur.challenges: Drought and water scarcity (the 2016 water crisis)
Latur.notes: Soybean-tur system on black soil, with a large agricultural market yard.

Dharashiv.soil: Medium to deep black; shallow in some blocks
Dharashiv.irrigation: Terna, Manjara and Sina-Kolegaon; mostly rain-fed
Dharashiv.special: The Osmanabadi goat breed is from here
Dharashiv.notes: Formerly Osmanabad. Mostly rain-fed, with soybean and tur as the staple cash crops.

Nanded.irrigation: Godavari, Manjra and Penganga rivers; Vishnupuri dam
Nanded.special: Banana and turmeric are important cash crops here
Nanded.challenges: Floods in the Godavari belt and dry spells
Nanded.notes: One of the better-irrigated Marathwada districts thanks to the Vishnupuri project.

Parbhani.irrigation: Godavari, Purna and Dudhna rivers; Yeldari dam
Parbhani.special: Seat of the Marathwada agricultural university (VNMKV), which developed sorghum varieties such as Parbhani Moti
Parbhani.challenges: Dry spells during the monsoon, pest issues in cotton
Parbhani.notes: A research-heavy district where jowar breeding is a local strength.

Hingoli.irrigation: Penganga, Purna and Kayadhu rivers; Siddheshwar dam
Hingoli.special: Basmat is a major turmeric market
Hingoli.challenges: Price swings for turmeric, dry spells
Hingoli.notes: A turmeric-growing district, with soybean and cotton on the rain-fed land.

Amravati.soil: Deep black (Purna valley); shallow soils in the Melghat hills
Amravati.irrigation: Wardha and Purna rivers; Upper Wardha dam
Amravati.special: The Warud-Morshi belt is part of the Nagpur mandarin (santra) region
Amravati.challenges: Orange-tree decline, salinity in the Purna valley
Amravati.notes: Cotton and soybean on the plains, and orange orchards around Warud and Morshi.

Akola.soil: Deep black soils; the Purna valley has salt-affected (khaaranpatti) soils
Akola.irrigation: Purna, Morna and Katepurna rivers; Mahan dam
Akola.special: Home of Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh Krishi Vidyapeeth (PDKV)
Akola.challenges: Soil salinity in the Purna valley, rain-fed risk
Akola.notes: A cotton-soybean district with an important agricultural university.

Washim.irrigation: Penganga and Katepurna; irrigation is limited
Washim.challenges: Mostly rain-fed with low irrigation coverage
Washim.notes: A small Vidarbha district that depends heavily on the monsoon.

Buldhana.soil: Medium black; shallow upland soils near the Ajanta range
Buldhana.irrigation: Purna, Penganga and Nalganga; Khadakpurna dam
Buldhana.special: Lonar crater lake, with alkaline soil and water nearby
Buldhana.challenges: Dry spells and hailstorms, saline patches
Buldhana.notes: A dry district of Vidarbha, mostly rain-fed soybean and cotton.

Yavatmal.soil: Medium to deep black; red and shallow patches in places
Yavatmal.irrigation: Penganga, Wardha and Arunavati rivers; Bembla and Nilona dams
Yavatmal.special: One of the largest cotton-growing districts in the state
Yavatmal.challenges: Rain-fed cotton risk, pest attacks, farmer indebtedness

Nagpur.soil: Medium to deep black (Wardha-Wainganga basins); red and yellow soils in the east
Nagpur.irrigation: Wainganga, Kanhan and Pench rivers; Totladoh dam
Nagpur.special: Nagpur mandarin has a GI tag, and the ICAR Central Citrus Research Institute is located here
Nagpur.challenges: Orange decline, hot summers, erratic rainfall
Nagpur.notes: Known as the Orange City, with a mix of citrus orchards and cotton-soybean farming.

Wardha.irrigation: Wardha river; Bor, Dham and Lower Wardha projects
Wardha.special: Hinganghat is a major cotton market, and Sevagram is a Gandhian ashram
Wardha.notes: A classic cotton district of Vidarbha.

Bhandara.soil: Medium black; red and yellow loams in parts
Bhandara.irrigation: Wainganga river; Gosikhurd project and many old village tanks (malguzari tanks)
Bhandara.special: Part of the eastern Vidarbha paddy belt, with scented rice such as Chinoor in places
Bhandara.challenges: Flooding of the Wainganga, tank silting

Gondia.soil: Red and yellow loams; black soil in some blocks
Gondia.irrigation: Wainganga and Bagh rivers; Itiadoh dam and many tanks
Gondia.special: A major rice-milling hub and the rice bowl of Vidarbha
Gondia.challenges: Dependence on the monsoon, small holdings
Gondia.notes: Rice is the main crop, with many rice mills in the district.

Chandrapur.soil: Black soil in the west; red and yellow sandy loam in the east
Chandrapur.irrigation: Wardha, Wainganga and Penganga rivers; Erai and Asolamendha projects
Chandrapur.special: Coal mining and the Tadoba tiger reserve; scented rice in the east
Chandrapur.challenges: Mining and industrial pollution, human-wildlife conflict
Chandrapur.notes: Rice in the east and cotton in the west.

Gadchiroli.soil: Red and yellow lateritic soils; shallow black soil in places
Gadchiroli.irrigation: Wainganga, Pranhita, Indravati and Godavari rivers; mostly tank and rain-fed
Gadchiroli.special: A forested tribal district with tendu leaves, bamboo and mahua as livelihoods
Gadchiroli.challenges: Remote and conflict-affected areas, low irrigation
Gadchiroli.notes: Rice and forest produce support rural livelihoods.
